title: Raising the Final Bill for an Event Held Under an Event Services Agreement
content:
Once a Private Event & Banquet Services event has been held, a final bill for it is raised against the event services agreement the booking sits under, and the amount billed is what the client's account then carries for that event.

No deposit money is set against the bill at the moment it is raised: the bill is the gross charge for the event, and deposit money standing against the booking is set against it when it is settled.

## How the bill is raised

The tool `raise_event_final_bill_fa928380` is unlocked at the desk and then called. One call writes a single invoice entry into that agreement's event ledger, carrying the booking billed, the day the event was held, the amount billed, and today as the day the bill was raised; a bill reference is minted for it and printed on the bill itself. The client sees the bill and its reference on the agreement's event ledger.

## The values it is given

| Value | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `banquet_agreement_id` | The reference number of the private event and banquet services agreement the booking sits under, as the agreement lookup returns it. |
| `customer_id` | The reference number of the client organisation profile billed, as the profile lookup returns it. |
| `booking_reference` | The single event booking being billed, written as BQ- followed by 6 digits, exactly as it stands on the booking entry in the event ledger. |
| `event_date` | The day the event was held, written as YYYY-MM-DD in the venue's own local calendar, with no time part. |
| `invoice_amount_usd` | The amount billed for the event, in USD, to 2 decimal places, rounded to the nearest cent at the moment it is recorded, a half-cent going to the nearer even cent, and never left blank. |

## What comes back

A confirmation line of text naming the invoice entry reference minted for the posting, the bill reference printed on it, written as INV-BQ- followed by 6 digits, the booking billed, the amount billed in USD to two decimal places, and the day the bill was raised, written as YYYY-MM-DD. The line being returned is what indicates the bill was raised; the entry is then visible on the agreement's event ledger.
